title: Multi-Pool Index Maintenance (Wave 2) — No-Throw Pool Open + EVERYTHING + Health Report + Logging
repo_context: Wave 2 focuses on operational contracts: safe pool-open boundary, EVERYTHING pool maintenance (head-only v0), stable pool health report, and structured logging.

stories.title: Add safe pool-open boundary: PoolOpenReport (OK|UNAVAILABLE) + stable reason codes (no-throw contract) + tests
acceptance_criteria: A typed PoolOpenReport exists with fields: status (OK|UNAVAILABLE), reason_code (DiagnosticReasonCode), detail (optional), action_hint (optional)
MaintenanceController (or a wrapper it calls) uses safe_open_pool(...) so UI/agent-facing maintenance calls do not throw for schema mismatch, missing artifacts, or open failures
Deterministic pytest: schema mismatch yields UNAVAILABLE_SCHEMA_VERSION_MISMATCH with action_hint REBUILD_POOL
Deterministic pytest: generic open failure yields UNAVAILABLE_UNKNOWN (or the closest existing stable reason code)
stories.notes: Pool-open is an orchestrator boundary concern. SliceDiagnoser/SliceExecutor should remain pure and not open files.

stories.title: Make multi-pool selection explicit: maintenance surfaces accept pool_identifier + explicit view mapping + tests
acceptance_criteria: Diagnose/execute entry points do not default to FINAL implicitly; view selection is explicit and tested
A deterministic pytest shows that selecting pool_identifier EVERYTHING uses CorpusView.EVERYTHING inventory and does not enumerate FINAL slices
stories.notes: Either pass both (pool_identifier + CorpusView) or implement a tiny explicit mapping layer; avoid hidden defaults.

stories.title: EVERYTHING pool inventory/diagnose/execute (head-only v0) end-to-end + deterministic tests
acceptance_criteria: Inventory for CorpusView.EVERYTHING emits entry_id values in head-form draft_id format: draft:head:<dossier_id>:<transcription_id>
desired_signature for EVERYTHING slices equals hydrated entry.content_hash
Diagnose for EVERYTHING returns expected statuses (MISSING/STALE/HEALTHY/UNAVAILABLE) using indexed_entry_state comparisons
Execute rebuilds exactly one EVERYTHING entry slice (delete_entry_slice + rebuild + update state) without touching other slices
Deterministic tests cover the above without network calls or external server dependency
stories.notes: No parallel drafts ingestion this wave. Keep semantics strictly head-only v0.

stories.title: Expose stable PoolHealthReport shape (reuse existing stats/should_compact) + tests
acceptance_criteria: When pool open succeeds, the maintenance surface returns a PoolHealthReport with: active_vectors, tombstoned_vectors, tombstone_ratio, compact_recommended (and optional threshold)
Implementation reuses existing stats logic and should_compact() (no duplicate computation logic)
Deterministic pytest: health report fields exist when pool opens; compaction recommendation toggles when threshold is crossed (stubbed is acceptable)
stories.notes: Only include slice_diagnoses when pool open succeeded; pool_open report is always present.

stories.title: Replace stderr prints with structured logging in maintenance paths (no behavior change) + tests (if applicable)
acceptance_criteria: Index maintenance paths no longer use print(..., file=sys.stderr); they use the repo logger
Logs include useful fields where possible: pool_identifier, dossier_id, entry_id, operation, exception_type
stories.notes: Do not add heavy dependencies. Use existing logging conventions configured in the repo.
